units.source_excerpt: Recently, Wordle, a puzzle game, has been spreading widely around the world and has a high level of buzz on social media such as Twitter.
units.function: Open on the object, the verb of spread, and the platform where the buzz is measured.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the object, say it is spreading, then name the platform that records the spread.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open on the model.

units.source_excerpt: Understanding the spread mechanism of the Wordle craze and the factors influencing the difficulty of the game may shed some light on important issues such as understanding the viral spread in the Internet era and the way the human brain associates words.
units.function: Widen one game into two larger questions, and hedge the claim with may.
units.reusable_pattern: State the local mechanism, then the two larger issues it may illuminate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the game answers the larger question.

units.source_excerpt: We developed an epidemiology-like differential equation model describing the variation in the total number of reports based on the SIR model and fitted the model using a genetic algorithm to minimize the MSE.
units.function: Name the family, the base it comes from, the fitting tool, and the loss, in one sentence.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the family, the model it is based on, the algorithm, and the quantity minimized.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the algorithm without the loss.

units.source_excerpt: We then used the fitted model to make a point forecast of the total number of reports on March 1, 2023. To obtain confidence intervals for the predictions, we used the Bootstrap method.
units.function: Separate the point forecast from the interval, and give the interval its own method.
units.reusable_pattern: State the point, then open a new sentence on the interval and name its method.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let the point and the interval share a method.

units.source_excerpt: To improve the speed of fitting the Bootstrap sample, we used the computationally faster Nelder-Mead method, based on the same initial parameters optimized by a genetic algorithm.
units.function: Justify a cheaper optimizer by speed, and tie it to the initial point already found.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the speed problem, the faster method, and the initial point it inherits.
reusable_elements: based on the same initial parameters
prohibited_generalizations: Do not switch optimizers without saying why.

units.source_excerpt: The 1000 Bootstrap estimates were arranged from smallest to largest, and the 25th and 975th estimates were selected as the lower and upper bounds of the prediction interval.
units.function: State the interval rule as an ordering and two ranks, not as a formula.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the sample size, the ordering, and the two ranks that become the bounds.
reusable_elements: selected as the lower and upper bounds
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide the percentile rule inside a name.

units.source_excerpt: Two characteristic lexical internal features are built in this paper. We define regularity and purity (negentropy) features by assuming first-order Markovianity of the occurrence probability of characters in the English lexicon.
units.function: Announce the count of new features, then the assumption that defines them.
units.reusable_pattern: Say how many features, name them, and give the assumption in a by clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define a feature without the assumption behind it.

units.source_excerpt: All indications are that they are indeed related to the difficulty of the lexicon being guessed.
units.function: Claim a relation with a sweeping opener and an intensifier, and no number.
units.reusable_pattern: Open on the sweep, then the relation, and keep the number out.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat this sentence as a test result.

units.source_excerpt: KNN regression has the excellent property of ensuring that the predicted distribution still sums to zero, so we use the KNN regression model to make predictions about the distribution of Wordle scores.
units.function: Give the property first and the choice second, joined by so.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the property the method guarantees, then the decision it justifies.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not choose a method and explain it afterwards.

units.source_excerpt: The covariance matrix is widely used in this paper for initial selection of variables and determining the relationship between variables.
units.function: Name one tool and the two jobs it does across the paper.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the tool, say it is used widely, and list the two jobs.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce the tool inside each section that uses it.

units.source_excerpt: We used the median scores of Wordle players to measure the difficulty of the words in the puzzle, classifying the difficulty as 'easy', 'normal', and 'hard'.
units.function: Name the measure and the three labels in the same sentence.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the statistic, then the verb of classification, then the three quoted labels.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not announce labels before the measure.

units.source_excerpt: The results show that the features can effectively predict the difficulty classification of words.
units.function: Close a method paragraph with a bare effectiveness claim and no number.
units.reusable_pattern: Open on the results, then the claim, and leave the accuracy for the body.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not put the accuracy in the summary if the body has it.

units.source_excerpt: In further exploration of the data, our most important finding is that the variation in the percentage of Hard Mode shows a high degree of similarity to the variation in the faithful players assumed in our initially built contagion-like model, which somewhat corroborates the soundness of our model.
units.function: Rank one finding as the most important, compare two curves, and hedge the corroboration.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark the finding, compare the two series, and close with a hedged corroboration.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the curves prove the model.

units.source_excerpt: Thank you for your letter asking for information about your famous Wordle game.
units.function: Open the letter by thanking the reader for the letter that asked.
units.reusable_pattern: Thank the addressee, name the letter, and name the object.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open a letter on a result.

units.source_excerpt: Considering that it is a popular puzzle game worldwide, the analysis of its popularity trends and dissemination mechanism, as well as its word difficulty, is important not only for your company, but also for the dissemination of Internet trends in general and for the understanding of human language.
units.function: Widen the stake from the addressee to two larger fields, with not only and but also.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the popularity, then the local stake, then the two wider stakes.
information_order: concession, local stake, two wider stakes
reusable_elements: not only for your company, but also
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the work matters only to the addressee.

units.source_excerpt: First, the number of Wordle game scores uploaded on Twitter fits well with the traditional epidemic spread model; the difference is that epidemic patients eventually lose their ability to spread, while a fraction of Wordle players become veteran players who continue to play Wordle and spread related information.
units.function: Grant the fit, then spend the second half on the one difference.
units.reusable_pattern: State the agreement, then the difference, with while carrying the contrast.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the model is the epidemic model.

units.source_excerpt: If the number of results on Twitter is a true reflection of Wordle's hotness, then our epidemiology-like model tells us that Wordle has entered the tail end, or plateau, of its life cycle.
units.function: Condition the verdict on one premise the reader must accept.
units.reusable_pattern: State the premise, then the verdict, and offer the verdict as two nouns.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the condition.

units.source_excerpt: for example, we predict that the number of reports for March 1, 2023 is included in the interval [11173.04,17069.15] at a 95% confidence level.
units.function: Attach one number to the verdict with for example.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark the number as an example, then give the date, the interval, and the level.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not lead the letter with the number.

units.source_excerpt: we know from the model that in order to continue its spreading ability, you should broaden the user base - which, of course, is difficult; or you can try to increase the stickiness of loyal users to continue the life of the game.
units.function: Turn the model into two pieces of advice, and concede that the first is hard.
units.reusable_pattern: State the goal, the first option with its concession, then the second option.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give advice the model cannot reach.

units.source_excerpt: Regarding the issue of Hard Mode player ratio you mentioned; we conclude that the attributes of words do not affect this ratio.
units.function: Point back at the addressee's question, then give the negative in one clause.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the question as theirs, then the conclusion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the negative.

units.source_excerpt: Since players should not know the information about the word of the day until they try the game every day; and since the evolution of loyal players in our model is similar to the trend of this ratio, it may mean that the change in this ratio can be explained by the life cycle of the game alone.
units.function: Stack two since clauses, one about the players and one about the model, before the hedged reading.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the two reasons, then the reading with may.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop either reason.

units.source_excerpt: There may be some teams that believe that certain specific indicators of difficulty are related to this proportion, but that is likely because there is an overall trend in those characteristics over time, as is the case with the proportion of Hard Mode players, so statistical tools such as regression may misidentify this trend over time as a direct relationship between the two.
units.function: State the rival belief, give it a cause, and name the tool that would be fooled.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the rival, explain it by a shared trend, and name the tool.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not attack the rival without the mechanism.

units.source_excerpt: You have also asked us to predict the distribution of results for specific dates and specific words. Based on our experiments, the effect of considering the date factor is not significant, so we use only word information.
units.function: Repeat the request, report the dropped factor, and close with so.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate what was asked, say the date does nothing, then the decision.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop a factor silently.

units.source_excerpt: we average the outcome distributions of a number of words that are similar to the words you wish to predict as the predicted outcome.
units.function: Explain the method as averaging similar words, with no name attached.
units.reusable_pattern: Say what is averaged, the similarity, and that the average is the prediction.
reusable_elements: a number of words that are similar
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the algorithm in the letter if the body names it.

units.source_excerpt: The exact number of words to average and how the factors for evaluating similarity are chosen is determined by the machine through some testing methods.
units.function: Hand the two tuning choices to the machine and keep the testing unnamed.
units.reusable_pattern: List the two choices, then say the machine makes them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not pretend the counts were chosen by hand.

units.source_excerpt: For example, our distribution estimate for the word EERIE is (0.20 4.87 23.55 35.36 23.75 9.94 2.33). The prediction interval is around 5% above and below the predicted value - depending on the specific number of attempts.
units.function: Give the seven numbers in parentheses, then the interval as a width that depends.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark the example, list the seven values, then the width and its dependence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not print the interval as exact.

units.source_excerpt: The uncertainty in our predictions lies mainly in the fact that we do not deal with changes in player structure.
units.function: Locate the uncertainty in one omission, not in the fit.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the uncertainty, then the one thing left out.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not blame the data.

units.source_excerpt: We believe that the distribution of the number of guesses people make is an important indicator of the difficulty of a word. We therefore classify word difficulty accordingly into three categories: easy, moderate and difficult.
units.function: State the belief, then the classification, with therefore between them.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the belief, the therefore, and the three labels.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not classify without the belief.

units.source_excerpt: for example, we consider EERIE to be of average difficulty.
units.function: Give the label for the one word the addressee cares about.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark the example and give the label.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give the label without the example marker.

units.source_excerpt: The number of repeated letters, weighted purity and weighted regularity are related to the difficulty rating, with the first two positively correlated and the last two negatively correlated.
units.function: List the attributes, then split them into two correlation directions.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the attributes, then the positive group and the negative group.
prohibited_generalizations: The count of attributes and the count of directions do not match. Keep both.

units.source_excerpt: In addition to the issues you were interested in earlier, there are also some other insights, that may be useful to you.
units.function: Mark the extra findings as beyond the request, and hedge their use.
units.reusable_pattern: Point at their questions, then the extras, with may.
reusable_elements: in addition to the issues you were interested in
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present extras as answers.

units.source_excerpt: which means you can observe the trend of the challenge mode reporting ratio to determine the change of the wordle loyal player ratio and thus optimize your business strategy.
units.function: Turn a correlation into an action the addressee can take.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the observable, the inference, and the action.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the correlation.

units.source_excerpt: If you want to reduce the difficulty of the game to attract more players, you can increase the likelihood of players guessing the puzzle by indicating the number of repeating letters in the word at the time of play.
units.function: Offer the advice inside the addressee's own goal.
units.reusable_pattern: State their goal, then the action, then the mechanism.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give the action without their goal.

units.source_excerpt: Wordle is a puzzle game in which Players try to solve the puzzle by guessing a five-letter word in six tries or less, receiving feedback with every guess.
units.function: Define the game by the length, the limit, and the feedback.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the game, the word length, the try limit, and the feedback.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume the reader knows the rules.

units.source_excerpt: We are employed by the New York Times to use only the data they send us to analyze and answer following questions.
units.function: State the employer, the data restriction, and the job in one sentence.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the employer, the only data, and the task.
reusable_elements: use only the data they send us
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply outside data.

units.source_excerpt: How does the date and other factors influence the number of reported results? If a certain date is given, how to predict the number of reported results? (A prediction interval is asked)
units.function: Restate the question as two questions and keep the parenthetical demand.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the mechanism question, the prediction question, and the demanded interval.
reusable_elements: if a certain date is given
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the parenthetical.

units.source_excerpt: How to predict the distribution of tries if a certain date and solution word are given? What factors that can influence the result might be omitted?
units.function: Pair the prediction question with a question about what is left out.
units.reusable_pattern: Ask for the distribution, then ask what might be omitted.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not restate a task without its omission clause.

units.source_excerpt: How to measure difficulty? How to separate solution words into different groups according to their difficulty?
units.function: Split one task into the measure and the grouping.
units.reusable_pattern: Ask how to measure, then how to separate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the measure and the groups.

units.source_excerpt: Find interesting features in the data set!
units.function: Keep the open task as an imperative with its exclamation.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the imperative and stop.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not turn the open task into a list.

units.source_excerpt: Main assumptions are:
units.function: Announce the list as the main assumptions and stop.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the list and let the items follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not argue the assumptions in the announcement.

units.source_excerpt: Words in the given data are English words, thereby share some common probabilistic identities with other English words in dictionaries.
units.function: State the assumption and the consequence it buys, joined by thereby.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the fact assumed, then what it licenses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not state an assumption with no consequence.

units.source_excerpt: Words that look like valid English words are more easily remembered and given priority for trial.
units.function: State a behavior assumption as a comparative with no hedge.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the kind of word and the two advantages it gets.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften a behavior assumption that the model needs.

units.source_excerpt: Model-specific assumptions will be presented in subsequent sections.
units.function: Defer the rest of the assumptions and say where they go.
units.reusable_pattern: Name what is deferred and where it appears.
reusable_elements: will be presented in subsequent sections
prohibited_generalizations: Do not pretend the assumption list is complete.

units.source_excerpt: The primary notations used in this paper are listed in Table 1.
units.function: Point at the notation table and call the list primary.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the table and the scope.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define symbols in prose when a table holds them.

units.source_excerpt: While examining the dataset we found two types of outliers in the dataset: word lengths that are not 5 and an unusually low number of total reports.
units.function: Name the two kinds of outlier before the table.
units.reusable_pattern: Say what was found and list the two types.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not show the table first.

units.source_excerpt: To ensure the correctness of the data, we chose to use the removal of anomalous data instead of correction and interpolation.
units.function: State the choice and the two alternatives it refuses.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the goal, the choice, and the refused options.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not remove rows without naming the alternative.

units.source_excerpt: For KNN regression and classification, to avoid the effect of magnitudes on calculating the distance between observations, we normalized the data according to the following equation.
units.function: Tie the standardization to the one method it protects.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the method, the harm avoided, and the equation.
reusable_elements: to avoid the effect of magnitudes
prohibited_generalizations: Do not standardize without saying which method needs it.

units.source_excerpt: where x_ij is i-th observation of criteria j, X_j is all the observations of criteria j, x*_ij is normalized data. The normalized data had a mean of 0 and a variance of 1.
units.function: Define only the new symbols, then state the two moments the transform produces.
units.reusable_pattern: Define the symbols, then the mean and the variance.
reusable_elements: a mean of 0 and a variance of 1
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the result of a standardization unstated.

units.source_excerpt: In English, valid words usually have regular patterns of form, which are quite hard to capture and formalize by mankind, but it can influence the choices of people when playing Wordle, because those words that are regular may be more familiar to English users.
units.function: Concede that the pattern is hard to formalize, then say why it still matters.
units.reusable_pattern: Grant the difficulty, then the influence, then the reason.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the pattern is fully captured.

units.source_excerpt: Assuming that each character's probabilistic distribution is just determined by its previous character in the word, we try to model the process with a Bi-gram-like chain.
units.function: Put the Markov assumption in a participial clause before the model.
units.reusable_pattern: State the assumption, then the attempt and the family.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not state the model before the assumption.

units.source_excerpt: to make use of the information of the start and end of the word, we made two virtual characters BOW and EOW at the beginning and the end of the word.
units.function: Justify two invented symbols by the information they keep.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the information, the two symbols, and their positions.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent boundary symbols silently.

units.source_excerpt: Regularity is defined as the geometric mean of the probability of the transfer process of each character to its successor, as described by the formula.
units.function: Define the quantity in words before the formula.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the quantity, the operation, and point at the formula.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let the formula arrive unexplained.

units.source_excerpt: in which P(c_i | c_{i-1}), sometimes also denoted as P(T_i) in this paper, is used to represent the possibility of transition from character i - 1 to character i.
units.function: Give a symbol its second name in the same sentence that defines it.
units.reusable_pattern: Define the symbol, give the alias, and say what it represents.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce an alias later.

units.source_excerpt: If a character in the word is given, how much information can we gain about its succeeding character?
units.function: Open a definition with the question it answers.
units.reusable_pattern: Pose the question, then define.
reusable_elements: how much information can we gain
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open a definition on the formula.

units.source_excerpt: This is a significant factor in Wordle, because the game's feedback would tell us wether the guessed letter is actually in the word of the day, so if succeeding word is more unpredictable, it will to harder to solve the puzzle.
units.function: Justify the factor by the feedback the game gives, and keep the printed slips.
units.reusable_pattern: Call it significant, give the because, and the so.
prohibited_generalizations: The printed wether and it will to harder stay as printed.

units.source_excerpt: The purity of a character c_i is defined below.
units.function: Announce the definition and point down.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the quantity and the pointer.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not bury the announcement.

units.source_excerpt: that is, -Entro(c_{i+1}), with the assumption from section 3.1 that each character's probabilistic distribution is just determined by its previous character in the word.
units.function: Restate the formula as a named quantity and point back at the assumption.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the alias, then the assumption and its section.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not restate a formula without its assumption.

units.source_excerpt: The higher the purity of a character, the smaller the number of next characters inferred from that character and the higher the probability that some specific character will occur.
units.function: Read the quantity as a the-higher-the-smaller pair.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the increase, then the two consequences.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave a quantity without its direction.

units.source_excerpt: The probabilities and purities are generated from 5 letter words from bestwordlist.com, without any frequency weighting.
units.function: Name the source and the one thing the source does not do.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the corpus, the site, and the missing weight.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite a corpus without its limitation.

units.source_excerpt: The purity of word i is simply defined as the sum of the character purities.
units.function: Mark a definition as simple when it only adds.
units.reusable_pattern: Say it is simple, then the operation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dress up a sum.

units.source_excerpt: The repetition index of words includes two items: the number of repeated letters and the maximum number of repeated letters.
units.function: Announce an index as two named items.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the index and the two items.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the count and the maximum.

units.source_excerpt: For example, there are no repeated letters except 'p' in 'apple', so the number of repeated letters in 'apple' is 1.
units.function: Teach the definition with one word and the count it produces.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the word, the letter, and the count after so.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define a count without an example.

units.source_excerpt: The effect of word repetition on the difficulty of Wordle is obvious.
units.function: Call an effect obvious before explaining it.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the effect and stop.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use obvious for a result that was tested.

units.source_excerpt: Wordle will only provide information about whether the answer word contains the input letter and whether the letter is in the correct position, but not whether the letter is repeated or the number of times it is repeated.
units.function: List what the feedback gives and, with but not, what it withholds.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the two things told, then the two things withheld.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe feedback without its gap.

units.source_excerpt: It is a reasonable assumption that people will preferentially think of those words in the available word space that they are most familiar with, regardless of whether the choice is constrained by available information.
units.function: Call the assumption reasonable and close with regardless.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark it reasonable, state the behavior, and name what does not change it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not state the assumption as a finding.

units.source_excerpt: For word frequency, we simply used a frequency list by Dave Hermit, whose corpus sources are movie subtitles.
units.function: Credit the list, the person, and the corpus in one sentence.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark it simple, name the source, and the corpus.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite a list without its corpus.

units.source_excerpt: notably that when training weighted version, log function is used to avoid float underflow, so the frequency of zero are set to 1 to avoid arithmetic problems.
units.function: Record a numerical fix and the problem it avoids.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark it as notable, name the fix, and the failure avoided.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide a floor of one inside the code.

units.source_excerpt: Purity is trained on a some word list with similar method with Regularity.
units.function: Point a second feature back at the first one's method.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the feature and the method it borrows.
prohibited_generalizations: The printed a some stays as printed.

units.section: 4.1 Intuition: What is in the Trend
units.source_excerpt: To give a thorough picture of how the number of reported results varies, we analyze the trend by hand, and have drawn some simple conclusions.
units.function: Say the first look was done by hand and the conclusions are simple.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the goal, the method, and the modesty of the result.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open a model section on the model.

units.section: 4.1 Intuition: What is in the Trend
units.source_excerpt: First, there is no periodicity in the trend that is visible to the naked eye.
units.function: Report a negative from inspection before any test.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the negative and the instrument, which is the eye.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the inspection.

units.section: 4.1 Intuition: What is in the Trend
units.source_excerpt: Given the characteristics of small games, weekly frequency periodicity is possible, but we found no periodicity under weekly frequency when we used the F-test.
units.function: Grant the expected period, then the test that finds none.
units.reusable_pattern: State the expectation, the but, and the test.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the test without the expectation.

units.section: 4.1 Intuition: What is in the Trend
units.source_excerpt: The overall trend consists of a relatively steep upward segment and a long-tailed downward segment, and the sequence is rather smooth.
units.function: Describe a curve as two segments and one texture.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the rise, the fall, and the smoothness.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe a curve with only one adjective.

units.section: 4.1 Intuition: What is in the Trend
units.source_excerpt: These properties are too obvious to be negligible.
units.function: Promote a description into a requirement with too obvious to.
units.reusable_pattern: Point back and refuse to drop it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip from description to model.

units.section: 4.1 Intuition: What is in the Trend
units.source_excerpt: And speaking in terms of mechanism, the spread of the behavior of playing Wordle and sharing scores can be very viral, so we take a epidemiology-like approach to model the process.
units.function: Separate the shape argument from the mechanism argument with and speaking.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark the shift, give the mechanism, and the so.
reusable_elements: and speaking in terms of mechanism
prohibited_generalizations: The printed a epidemiology stays as printed.

units.source_excerpt: We define terminologies of this section as follows.
units.function: Fence the jargon to one section.
units.reusable_pattern: Say the definitions hold here.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let section jargon leak.

units.source_excerpt: TP Twittering Playing: the behavior of playing Wordle and twittering about it.
units.function: Define a coined abbreviation as the behavior, not the person.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the short form, the expansion, and the behavior.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not coin an abbreviation without the expansion.

units.source_excerpt: TPers do TP everyday, and non-TPers, including those who transformed from TPers, never do TP.
units.function: State a consistency assumption as a pair of absolutes.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the always group and the never group.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften a consistency assumption.

units.source_excerpt: the probability of non-TPers transforming into TPers is determined by the number of TPers they may contact with.
units.function: Tie a probability to a contact count.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the probability and the count that sets it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the infection term unexplained.

units.source_excerpt: while some non-TPers have the possibility to transform into TPers, other non-TPers may not be possible to become TPers.

units.reusable_pattern: Give the convertible group and the closed group.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the whole population as convertible.

units.source_excerpt: non-TPers transformed from TPers will never become TPers again.
units.function: Close the loop with never again.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the group and the permanent state.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a return the model forbids.

units.source_excerpt: A basic SIR Model consists of a system of four differential equations.
